history.period: 18th century (present structures); shrine traditions traced to c. 13th century
history.summary: One of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva, in the village of Bhorgiri/Bhimashankar in Khed taluka, deep in the Sahyadri hills at ~1230 m. Legend says Shiva, as Bhimashankar, slew the demon Tripurasura here, and his sweat formed the Bhima River, which originates nearby and flows to merge with the Krishna. The temple is Nagara style; the present sabhamandap was built in the 18th century by Nana Phadnavis of the Peshwa court, and the shikhara by Nana Phadnavis as well. The Maratha-era history includes a large bell contributed by Chimaji Appa (brother of Bajirao I) and the grant of Kharosi village by Chhatrapati Shivaji; Shivaji, Rajaram Maharaj and Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath are recorded as visitors. Notes: (1) coordinates are approximate, taken from published listings; (2) some traditions locate the Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga at Dakini near Guwahati, Assam — the Maharashtra shrine is the most widely recognized.

name: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Bhimashankar is a hill settlement in the Sahyadri range of Pune district, around 110 km from Pune, set in dense forest within the Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary. It is famous as the source of the Bhima River and one of the twelve Jyotirlinga pilgrimage sites, drawing devotees, trekkers, and nature lovers. The surrounding sanctuary is known for the Indian giant squirrel and rich biodiversity of the Western Ghats.

travel.railway: Pune Junction, ~110 km by road (verify); nearest railhead for trekkers is Karjat (~75 km) via Khandas (verify)
travel.road: ~110 km from Pune via Manchar on NH60 (verify); buses and taxis available; trek routes Ganesh Ghat and Shidi Ghat from Khandas (34 km from Karjat)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan and Mahashivratri are spiritually significant but very crowded
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM to 9:30 PM daily (Kakad Aarti 4:30 AM, evening Aarti 7:30 PM); closed ~45 min for Madhyan Aarti around 3:00 PM (verify exact schedule at temple)
